You are ONE of three INDEPENDENT judges of a completed debate. You have not seen the other judges and you will not. Judge only what is in the transcript below. You are bound by the same layer rules as all debate participants, and by the same rulebook as every other judge of this debate.

Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: absent from its quote: defender || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: absent from its quote: defender || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: defender, nathan, david || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: absent from its quote: defender || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: defender || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: absent from its quote: defender || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: no verbatim quote found
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: no verbatim quote found
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: inference || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: inference, father, line, house, fathers || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: inference, luke, ONLY, solomon || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 6: absent from its quote: conclusion || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. A grade that rests on a witness left unanswered counts only when that witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (md_notes_rulings 392).
BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. Never choose a standing, a count or a clause to agree with another line, a check or an expected result.
A SIDE WITH A COUNTED LINK IS NOT SELF-SUPPORTED. If CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, DEFENSE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge; if CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, CHALLENGE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge. SELF-SUPPORTED requires a count of 0 for that side: every premise listed against it exhibited its footing or was VOID.
Line 1: the verdict word first (HELD, PARTIAL or BROKEN), then 2-4 sentences with [L1][L2][L3][L4] tags.
Line 2, exactly: RESULT: DEFENDER WINS | CHALLENGER WINS | UNDERDETERMINED -- one sentence a reader with no background understands. BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS. Otherwise the RESULT is your judgment (Commitments 7 and 8): DEFENDER WINS when the verses of the record, read together line upon line, support the chain of the defender against the chain of the challenger; UNDERDETERMINED when, read together, they leave the topic open. The sentence gives the reason.
Line 3, exactly: CLAUSE: <BROKEN-1 | BROKEN-2 | PARTIAL-1 | PARTIAL-2 | HELD-1> -- n=<n> w=<w> k=<k>

Then SIX MORE mandatory lines, exactly in these forms:
KEYSTONE: D<n> -- WITHDRAWN | BROKEN | STANDS -- name the LAST declared link, Dn, which is the conclusion link, and give its state. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. An UNDERDETERMINED grade gives, after GROUND:, [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words both readings rest on>" and what the record leaves open. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** A biological father is a man whose seed begets the child. The KJV says the child Jesus was conceived in Mary, a virgin, "of the Holy Ghost" with no man's seed. Joseph was her husband and was supposed to be the father. He was not the one who begot the child.

## 1. Mary was a virgin when she conceived, and the conception came before any coming together

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
**[L2]** The word is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". Luke gives it twice in one verse, and the text calls Mary "the virgin".

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *sunelthein* (G4905, from *sunerchomai*) means "to come together". Matthew places the conception before that coming together, and *echousa* (G2192, in "found with child") means "having in the womb".

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." Hebrew *yada* (H3045), "to know", is the word for marital union, and conception follows it.
**[L2]** The Greek *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know", is the word in Luke 1:34. Mary's "I know not a man" thus states that no union with a man had occurred.
**[L4]** From Luke 1:34, Luke 1:27 and Genesis 4:1: Scripture's own pattern is that "knowing" precedes conceiving. Mary says she has not known a man, and Luke calls her a virgin. So the conception that follows was not by a man's seed.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *gennēthen* (from *gennaō*, G1080) means "begotten, conceived". The preposition is *ek* (G1537), "out of", marking source. The text puts the origin of what was begotten in her out of the Holy Ghost.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
**[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow", describes God's power covering her. The phrase "of thee" is *ek sou* (G1537), "out of you".
**[L4]** Matthew 1:20 names the Holy Ghost as the source of the begetting. Luke 1:35 joins that act with "therefore also" to the title "Son of God". The text thus gives a source for the begetting, and that source is not a human father.

## MY CHAIN (C1 to C4)

**C1. The promised seed is David's, out of his body, according to the flesh.**

- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The Greek is *osphys* (G3751), "loins; procreative power." It is the same word used at Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The Greek is *ek spermatos* (G4690, "seed") and *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh").
- **[L4]** Bowels, belly and loins are a father's members (2 Samuel 7:12; Psalm 132:11; Hebrews 7:10). Paul calls what came from them *sperma* "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). So the promise is met by a seed of the flesh passed down a fathers' line.

**C2. The line is reckoned by the father's house, and the house named is Joseph's.**

- **[L3]** Ezra 2:59 gives the reverse case: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel." The 1611 margin reads "[seed: or, pedigree]."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:4: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)". This is said of Joseph.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:5 and 1:36: Mary's kinswoman Elisabeth "[was] of the daughters of Aaron." Mary is called "thy cousin Elisabeth's" kin.
- **[L4]** Moses' law reckons a man by his father's house (Numbers 1:18). A man who could not show it was set aside (Ezra 2:59). The one Davidic house Luke assigns in the birth account is Joseph's (Luke 2:4). The only kin Luke gives Mary is of Aaron (Luke 1:5, 36). So the "evident" descent from Juda (Hebrews 7:14) is reckoned through Joseph.

**C3. The father is named in four registers.**

- **[L1]** Mary speaks in Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The Greek is *ho patēr sou* (G3962), "thy father."
- **[L3]** The narrator writes "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41). The Greek is *goneis*, "parents."
- **[L3]** The town asks: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42). A disciple says: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- **[L3]** The angel speaks in Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The 1611 margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]." Matthew 1:21 adds: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Naming the child is the father's act, as in Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."

**C4. The means of begetting is knowing, and the abstinence is bounded.**

- **[L1]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." The Hebrew is *yada'* (H3045), "know."
- **[L3]** Joseph and Mary are husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19) and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The Greek is *heōs hou* (G2193), "till." It is joined to *eginōsken*, the imperfect of *ginōskō* (G1097).

Joseph is husband in law from the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24). The abstinence of Matthew 1:25 is bounded by "till," which covers the pregnancy. ## 5. D3 and D4: the father's acts, and the sign child of Isaiah's day

**Naming is a father's act as well as a mother's.**

## 6. Close

The seed promised to David proceeds "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). The loins are the father's members: "they come out of the loins of Abraham" (Hebrews 7:5) and "he was yet in the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:10). Luke sets the house of David on Joseph (Luke 1:27; 2:4). Mary calls him "thy father" (Luke 2:48). The angel names him "thou son of David" in the same row as "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The Holy Ghost's verbs are power and presence (Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34). The begetting-title is set at the resurrection (Acts 13:33; Romans 1:4). Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David.

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** A biological father is a man whose seed begets the child. The KJV says the child Jesus was conceived in Mary, a virgin, "of the Holy Ghost" with no man's seed. Joseph was her husband and was supposed to be the father. He was not the one who begot the child.

## 1. Mary was a virgin when she conceived, and the conception came before any coming together

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
**[L2]** The word is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". Luke gives it twice in one verse, and the text calls Mary "the virgin".

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *sunelthein* (G4905, from *sunerchomai*) means "to come together". Matthew places the conception before that coming together, and *echousa* (G2192, in "found with child") means "having in the womb".

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." Hebrew *yada* (H3045), "to know", is the word for marital union, and conception follows it.
**[L2]** The Greek *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know", is the word in Luke 1:34. Mary's "I know not a man" thus states that no union with a man had occurred.
**[L4]** From Luke 1:34, Luke 1:27 and Genesis 4:1: Scripture's own pattern is that "knowing" precedes conceiving. Mary says she has not known a man, and Luke calls her a virgin. So the conception that follows was not by a man's seed.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *gennēthen* (from *gennaō*, G1080) means "begotten, conceived". The preposition is *ek* (G1537), "out of", marking source. The text puts the origin of what was begotten in her out of the Holy Ghost.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
**[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow", describes God's power covering her. The phrase "of thee" is *ek sou* (G1537), "out of you".
**[L4]** Matthew 1:20 names the Holy Ghost as the source of the begetting. Luke 1:35 joins that act with "therefore also" to the title "Son of God". The text thus gives a source for the begetting, and that source is not a human father.

## 3. Joseph is husband and supposed father, but he is not said to have begotten Jesus

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
**[L2]** In the genealogy the verb *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat", runs through each line from father to son. At the last link the pattern changes. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary", and the one "of whom" Jesus was born is *hēs* (feminine singular, "of her"). Jesus is born of Mary and is not said to be begotten by Joseph.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
**[L2]** *enomizeto* (from *nomizō*, G3543) means "was supposed, thought". The text marks Joseph's fatherhood as a supposition and does not state it as a fact.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
**[L3]** Genesis 4:1 (above) shows "knew" as the act that precedes conceiving. Matthew 1:25 says Joseph did not know Mary before the birth.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L4]** From Matthew 1:19 and Matthew 1:20: Joseph is troubled over her pregnancy, and an angel must tell him "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". That shows he had no knowledge of having fathered the child. The angel's word gives the true source and settles the matter.

**[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?"
**[L3]** In Luke 2:48 Mary says "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". In Luke 2:49 the child answers by pointing to another father, whose business he must be about. Mary's phrase is the ordinary description of Joseph's household role. The child's reply names a different father.

## 4. The Scripture's earlier word points to a seed of the woman and a virgin's son

**[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head."
**[L2]** *zera* (H2233), "seed", is attached here to the woman alone.

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
**[L3]** Matthew 1:23 quotes it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son... God with us." The KJV's "virgin" in Matthew 1:23 is *parthenos* (G3933). The Hebrew standing behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *almah* (H5959).
**[L4]** From Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23: Matthew cites the sign as fulfilled in the birth he has just described. The sign is a virgin conceiving, so the prophecy needs no human father.

**[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me."
**[L2]** *katartizō* (G2675), "to prepare, fit", is the word behind "hast thou prepared".
**[L3]** John 1:14: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us."
**[L4]** Hebrews 10:5 says God prepared the body. John 1:14 says the Word became flesh. Together they show the body came by God's preparation and not by a father's begetting.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Mary was a virgin when she conceived, and the conception preceded any coming together with Joseph. Footing: Luke 1:27 "To a virgin espoused" with G3933 *parthenos* (virgin); Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" with G4905 *sunelthein* (to come together); Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man" with Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived".
2. The begetting is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost", not of a man. Footing: Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" with G1080 *gennaō* (begotten) and G1537 *ek* (out of); Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God" with G1982 *episkiazō* (overshadow).
3. Joseph is husband and supposed father only and is not the begetter. Footing: Matthew 1:16 "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" with the feminine *hēs* (of her) breaking the "begat" pattern; Luke 3:23 "as was supposed the son of Joseph" with G3543 *nomizō* (suppose); Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth"; Luke 2:49 "my father's business".
4. The earlier Scripture points to a seed of the woman and a virgin's son, and Matthew cites it as fulfilled. Footing: Genesis 3:15 "thy seed and her seed" with H2233 *zera* (seed); Isaiah 7:14 "a virgin shall conceive" with H5959 *almah* behind the KJV "virgin"; Matthew 1:23 "a virgin shall be with child".
5. The body of Christ came by God's preparation and not by a father's begetting. Footing: Hebrews 10:5 "a body hast thou prepared me" with G2675 *katartizō* (prepare); John 1:14 "the Word was made flesh".
6. Christ had no biological father. Footing: Links 1–5, namely the virgin conception before any union (Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:18), the Holy Ghost as the stated source (Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35), Joseph as husband and supposed father only (Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23), and the prophecy of the virgin's son (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:23).

I begin with the question, then take the presses D1 to D6 in order. Where a row cuts against a footing of mine I say so and name what I rest on instead.

---

## ANSWER TO THE QUESTION: how is it "evident" that he sprang out of Juda?

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
**[L2]** "Sprang" is *anatetalken* (from *anatellō*, G393), "to rise up". The same verb stands at Matthew 5:45: "for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good." Hebrews 7:14 says the Lord "sprang out of Juda", a rising out of the tribe. The word for "evident" is *prodēlon* (G4271), "openly evident". What the verse states as evident is a manifest rising out of the tribe of Juda. The way that rising is shown is the reckoning by the house, given next.

**The pedigree law is met by the house he was reckoned into.**
**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS." **[L3]** Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David."
**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543). You gloss it "properly, to do by law (usage)", and I take your gloss. A reckoning by law or usage is a reckoning made by the house. It is not a statement that the man begat.
**[L4]** Numbers 1:18 sets "the house of their fathers" as the reckoning. Joseph took the child into his house and named him (Matthew 1:20, 24-25), and Luke 3:23 reports that reckoning as "supposed". So the "evident" descent of Hebrews 7:14 is met by the house, and it needs no begetting by Joseph. Your own gloss of *enomizeto* carries the point.

**Two fathers for Joseph show that "son" is reckoned in these rows.**
**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph." **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli."
**[L2]** *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat", is the verb at every step in Matthew. In Luke 3:23 the brackets mark "[the son]" as the KJV's supplied words. The Greek chain is a run of "of"s, with *huios* (G5207, "son", which the lexicon says is used "of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship") standing once at the head.
**[L3]** Ezra 2:61: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name."
**[L4]** Joseph is "begat" of Jacob (Matthew 1:16) and "of Heli" (Luke 3:23). Both cannot be begetting. The KJV itself shows a man called by his wife's father's name (Ezra 2:61). So one of Joseph's two lines is reckoned by marriage, and the line through Heli to "[the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David" (Luke 3:31) is the line for Mary's side. This is an [L4] resting on Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23, 3:31 and Ezra 2:61.

**Mary's kinship to Elisabeth does not bar Juda.**
**[L3]** Luke 1:5 and 1:36 name Elisabeth "of the daughters of Aaron" and Mary her "cousin". **[L3]** 2 Chronicles 22:11: "the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest."
**[L4]** A daughter of the king of Juda was wife to a priest (2 Chronicles 22:11). So kin to a priest's wife is no proof Mary was not of Juda. Your C2 [L4] ("the only kin Luke gives Mary is of Aaron") stands on Luke 1:5, 36 alone and is a single layer.

**[L3]** Luke 1:32, said to Mary: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." **[L2]** *patēr* (G3962), "father", which the lexicon glosses "literally or figuratively, near or more remote". David is called the father of a child announced to Mary in 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

---

## D1: Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:18

**Granted:** *ginōskō* is present and the conception is future (Luke 1:31). I do not rest on tense alone.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" **[L1]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."
**[L3]** Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." The KJV defines "virgin" by "known", the same word-field (H3045 *yada*, "know") as Mary's "I know not a man". Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin" twice in one verse.
**[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know", with its present tense in Luke 1:34. It states her condition at the espousal, which is the very time of your row, Luke 1:27.
**[L4]** The only voice recorded from inside the espousal on the matter of knowing is Mary's, and it states that she does not know a man (Luke 1:34, Genesis 24:16). Your C4 supplies from the espousal a knowing that no quoted word of that espousal states. What it quotes are rows of status, not act. See C4 below.

**The answer given is a source.**
**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
**[L1]** Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
**[L4]** Mary asks how (Luke 1:34). The words that follow give the Holy Ghost coming and the power of the Highest overshadowing (1:35), and then ground the answer in "with God nothing shall be impossible" (1:37). The angel names God's act as the how. This stands on Luke 1:35 and 1:37 together with the question in 1:34.

**Matthew 1:18 and the taking (1:24).** I grant that "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24, *parelabe*, G3880) can be what "came together" means. It makes no difference to the source.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." The source is given in Matthew's own narration, before any angel speaks.
**[L3]** Luke 2:5: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." After the taking (Matthew 1:24) Luke still says "espoused".
**[L4]** The finding is dated before the taking (Matthew 1:18, 24). The birth narrative's own order is finding, then the angel's word (1:20), then the taking (1:24), then "knew her not till she had brought forth" (1:25). The child was already "found" in her before any taking. Your order, "espousal, finding, taking, till", puts the conception before the taking, which is my point.

---

## D2: "of the Holy Ghost"

**The verse whole, with the margin you gave.**
**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [conceived: Gr. begotten]
**[L2]** *gennēthen* (G1080). The lexicon: "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". *Ek* (G1537), "out of". The verb whose proper subject is the father is here given the Holy Ghost as its source, with the object "in her".
**[L4]** Matthew 1:20 gives the begetting-verb of the thing in her womb its source in the Holy Ghost. The lexicon's "properly, of the father" and the margin "begotten" are the two footings. The sentence names no man as source of "that which is conceived in her".

**Your 1 John 5:1 and 3:9.**
**[L1]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." **[L3]** 1 John 3:9: "for his seed remaineth in him."
**[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) is glossed in the lexicon "figuratively, to regenerate". In 1 John the birth is tied to "believeth" (*pisteuō*, G4100) and to "his seed" (God's).
**[L4]** In 1 John the birth from God is a second birth of one who believes. The seed there is God's seed ("his seed", 3:9). In Matthew 1:20 the object is "that which is conceived in her", a thing in the womb, and the source named is the Holy Ghost. The same preposition in both places does not make the objects the same. 1 John 3:9 gives "seed" to God, so the parallel supports a source in God and does not make the source stand beside another seed.

**Your Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, Acts 5:15.**
**[L2]** *eperchomai* (G1904), "come upon", and *episkiazō* (G1982), "overshadow", I grant as verbs of power resting.
**[L1]** Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The stated result is "power", for witness.
**[L1]** Luke 1:35: the stated result of the same verbs is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
**[L4]** The verbs are the same, but the stated result differs by verse. In Acts 1:8 the result is power for witness. In Luke 1:35 the result is a birth, given as the answer to a question about conceiving (Luke 1:34). A verb's meaning is fixed by its verse's stated result.

**Luke 1:35 "therefore" (*dio kai*).**
**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
**[L4]** "Therefore" follows the two clauses just before it in the same sentence (Holy Ghost come upon, power overshadow). The title is grounded in those two, not left standing on 1:32. You say it reaches back to 1:32, but 1:32 is the promise, and 1:34-35 is the question and the answer about how.

**Your 1 Chronicles 28:6 and 2 Samuel 7:14.**
**[L1]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
**[L2]** *bāchar* (H977), "choose, select". Solomon's sonship to God is stated as a choosing out of David's sons.
**[L1]** Luke 1:35 gives the ground of the title in the Holy Ghost's coming and overshadowing. Solomon's ground is election, Christ's is the conception.
**[L4]** Solomon is "chosen" (H977) from among David's sons, so David is the begetter and God the father by choice (1 Chronicles 28:6). In Luke 1:35 the title rests on the conception ("therefore also"). The two rows give different grounds for the title.

**Your Romans 1:3-4.**
**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690), "seed". I do not deny it. David's seed came to the child. The question is the line, and Mary's side answers it: "born of thee" (Luke 1:35, *ek sou*, "out of thee") puts the flesh out of Mary, and Luke 3:23-31 and Luke 1:32 give her David.

---

## D3: Joseph "supposed"

**Matthew 1:16.** I grant that "born of women" is said of men who have fathers (Matthew 11:11, Luke 1:13). I do not rest 1:16 on "of whom" alone. 1:16 is a witness to the shift in verb (*egennēsen*, "begat", to the passive with the woman). The weight is carried by Matthew 1:18 and 1:20, answered above.

**Luke 3:23.** See the answer to the question. Your gloss "by law (usage)" is a reckoning, not a claim of begetting. **[L1]** The parenthesis "(as was supposed)" stands in the same verse before "the son of Joseph".

**Luke 2:33, 43 and the "parents" rows.**
**[L1]** Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him." **[L1]** Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not of it."
**[L4]** Luke's own narration in 2:33 and 2:43 names the two as "Joseph and his mother". "His parents" (Luke 2:27, 41, *goneis*, "parents") is the household term. Luke's own voice marks the reckoning "supposed" at 3:23. John 1:45 and 6:42 are the speech of persons ("whose father and mother we know", the crowd that goes on to doubt his words), which is the reckoning Luke 3:23 calls "supposed".

**Luke 2:48-49.**
**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
I grant that Mary calls Joseph "thy father" in her own household speech. The child's reply names another Father in the next verse. Your rows (Luke 2:51, 2 Samuel 7:14) show the child "subject unto them", which I grant. Subjection to a household is not a statement of begetting.

**Matthew 1:19-20.**
**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "was minded to put her away privily." **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *gar* (G1063), "for", in 1:20 gives the ground of the command. The ground the angel gives for removing his fear is the source of what is in her.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child". **[L2]** *heurethē* (G2147), "was found", marks discovery.
**[L4]** The thing found (1:18), the intent it raised (1:19), and the ground that answers the intent (1:20) form one sequence. The ground is the origin "of the Holy Ghost". Your reading says the remedy is fear removed and wife taken, which I grant. The question is what removes the fear, and the verse states it as the origin clause. I withdraw my opening's phrase that Joseph "had no knowledge of having fathered the child". The row bears only what 1:18-20 state, and I rest on that.

**Naming.**
**[L1]** Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father." **[L1]** Luke 1:60: "his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John." **[L3]** Genesis 4:25: "she bare a son, and called his name Seth." **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt call his name JESUS", said to Mary.
**[L4]** Naming is done by the mother (Luke 1:60, Genesis 4:25), and Luke 1:31 gives it to Mary. So "thou shalt call" in Matthew 1:21 is no mark of begetting. Matthew 1:25, "he called his name JESUS", is the house-taking act I name above.

---

## D4: "her seed", Isaiah 7:14

**Genesis 3:15 and "seed".** I grant Genesis 4:25 and 16:10. "Her seed" is said of women whose sons have fathers. So Genesis 3:15 alone does not settle the means. It sets the line as the woman's. I rest the means on Luke 1:34-35 and Matthew 1:18-25.

**Isaiah 7:14 and 8:3.**
**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." **[L1]** Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled ... Behold, a virgin shall be with child."
**[L1]** Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz."
**[L4]** Isaiah's own text distinguishes two women ("a virgin", 7:14; "the prophetess", 8:3) and two names (Immanuel; Mahershalalhashbaz). The fulfilment is set by Matthew 1:22 on "all this", which includes "of the Holy Ghost" (1:18, 20) and "before they came together" (1:18). Matthew's own "virgin" (*parthenos*, G3933) is set beside "of the Holy Ghost" in the birth he is explaining. I grant the margin "Heb. approached" at 8:3 and that H5959 is "maid" and "damsels" elsewhere in the KJV. The KJV's own word in 7:14 and in Matthew 1:23 is "virgin", and Genesis 24:16 defines that word by "known".

---

## D5: "a body hast thou prepared me"

I grant Psalm 139:13 and Jeremiah 1:5. God's covering and forming is said of men who have fathers. So Hebrews 10:5 and John 1:14 do not by themselves exclude a father. I withdraw Link 5 as an independent proof. It stands only as consistent with Links 1 to 3, and the weight rests on those.

---

## D6: the keystone

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12, Psalm 132:11, Acts 2:30, Hebrews 7:10, Romans 1:3 give a seed from David's body.
**[L2]** *osphys* (G3751), "loins", and *sperma* (G4690), "seed".
**[L4]** Your C1 shows the promise runs through David's body. It does not show which parent of the promised child carries it. 2 Samuel 7:14 speaks of the first fulfilment in a son who "commit[s] iniquity", so it speaks of the line. Acts 2:30 has God "raise up Christ" (*anistēmi*, "to raise up") from the fruit of his loins. Luke 1:32 gives the throne of "his father David" to the child Mary is to conceive (1:31), and "born of thee" (Luke 1:35, *ek sou*, "out of thee") puts the flesh out of Mary. Her line is in Luke 3:23-31. So the promise is met by flesh of David's seed out of the mother. C1's [L4] ("bowels, belly and loins are a father's members") assumes the child's David-flesh passes by the father. Hebrews 7:10 says only that Levi was in the loins of his ancestor, and it says nothing about Joseph.

---

## C4: the "union within the espousal"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20 calls her "thy wife". **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L2]** *heōs hou* (G2193), "until". *Eginōsken* (G1097), "knew", imperfect, continuing action.
**[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:24 names a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (*rēa'*, H7453, "neighbour").
**[L4]** Matthew 1:20 calls her "thy wife", and Matthew 1:25 within the same chapter says he "knew her not" until the birth. So the KJV itself sets the name "wife" beside a state of not knowing. The rows you give for C4 (Matthew 1:19-20, Deuteronomy 22:24) are rows of status, and Matthew 1:20, 25 show that status and act are separate in this very account. What follows "till" is after the birth, so it falls outside the conception. The child was "found" in her before the taking (1:18, 24).

---

## STATE OF MY CHAIN

My weight stands on Links 1 to 3 and 6: Luke 1:27, 34, 35, 37; Matthew 1:18, 20, 25; Luke 3:23; with Genesis 24:16 and 4:1 fixing the word "know". Genesis 3:15 and Hebrews 10:5 are consistent with those links and I do not offer them as proof of the means. Luke 3:23-31 and Ezra 2:61 are the footing for Mary's line, and that is an [L4].

**ANSWER: Isaiah 8:3, Isaiah 8:4 and Isaiah 8:18 -- D4 --** "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." "I and the children whom the LORD hath given me [are] for signs and for wonders in Israel."
- [L3] Isaiah 8:8: "O Immanuel."
- [L4] The child of Isaiah 8:3 is named Mahershalalhashbaz by command. The child of Isaiah 7:14 is named Immanuel. Isaiah 8:8 addresses the land as "thy land, O Immanuel". The Immanuel of Isaiah 7:14 is a different child from the one of 8:3. Isaiah's children are signs (8:18), and the sign of 7:14 is the virgin's, which Matthew 1:23 applies.

**ANSWER: Genesis 24:16, Genesis 24:43 and Romans 9:10 -- D4 --** "a virgin, neither had any man known her." "when Rebecca also had conceived by one, [even] by our father Isaac."
- [L2] *'almah* (H5959) at Genesis 24:43.
- [L4] The challenger's Rebekah is a virgin at the hour she is called one, since "neither had any man known her" (Genesis 24:16). When she conceives, Romans 9:10 names her husband, "by one, even by our father Isaac". In Matthew 1:20 the source is named "of the Holy Ghost". The two named sources differ, and the verses name both.

**ANSWER: Exodus 2:8 -- D4 --** "And the maid went and called the child's mother."
- [L2] *'almah* (H5959) names the maid.
- [L4] The word names a maiden. It is rendered "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14, and Matthew 1:23 renders it by *parthenos*.

---

## D5

**ANSWER: Galatians 4:4 and Matthew 11:11 -- D5 --** "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." "Among them that are born of women."
- [L2] *ginomai* (G1096, "to become").
- [L4] I grant that "of a woman" is said of men with fathers, so I do not rest the source on those words. D5 rests on Hebrews 10:5 and Matthew 1:20.

**ANSWER: Hebrews 10:5 -- D5 --** "but a body hast thou prepared me."
- [L2] *katartizō* (G2675, "to fit, complete, prepare").
- [L3] John 1:14: "And the Word was made flesh."
- [L4] The one who cometh into the world speaks of a body "prepared" for him. The preparing is God's act ("thou hast prepared"). Together with Matthew 1:20, the body's source is stated as God's preparation and the Holy Ghost.

**ANSWER: John 1:6 -- D5 --** "There was a man sent from God, whose name [was] John."

## D6

- [L4] The source is stated twice, once by the narrator and once by the angel, and it is the Holy Ghost. The line shifts from "begat" to "of whom was born" exactly at Jesus. Joseph is "husband" and "supposed" father. Christ had no biological father.

# CHALLENGE, ROUND 1: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David

**Position.** The seed promised to David comes "out of thy bowels" and is "according to the flesh." The tribe is reckoned "by the house of their fathers." The man the text names as husband, as father, and as "of the house of David" is Joseph. The Holy Ghost rows in Matthew and Luke name the covenant origin, the power and the title. They sit in the same verses that name Joseph and the throne "of his father David." I answer each of D1 to D6 at the word level. I aim at the keystone, D6, through the links it stands on.

---

## MY CHAIN (C1 to C4)

**C1. The promised seed is David's, out of his body, according to the flesh.**

- **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
- **[L2]** The word is *zera'* (H2233), "seed; posterity." The verb is *yatsa'*, "come forth." Its source is *me'eh*, "bowels, belly."
- **[L3]** Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." The 1611 margin reads "[body: Heb. belly]."
- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The Greek is *osphys* (G3751), "loins; procreative power." It is the same word used at Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The Greek is *ek spermatos* (G4690, "seed") and *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh").
- **[L4]** Bowels, belly and loins are a father's members (2 Samuel 7:12; Psalm 132:11; Hebrews 7:10). Paul calls what came from them *sperma* "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). So the promise is met by a seed of the flesh passed down a fathers' line.

**C2. The line is reckoned by the father's house, and the house named is Joseph's.**

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- **[L3]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." The Hebrew is *beit avotam*: *bayith* (H1004), "house, family," with *'ab* (H1), "father."
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:59 gives the reverse case: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel." The 1611 margin reads "[seed: or, pedigree]."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:4: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)". This is said of Joseph.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:5 and 1:36: Mary's kinswoman Elisabeth "[was] of the daughters of Aaron." Mary is called "thy cousin Elisabeth's" kin.
- **[L4]** Moses' law reckons a man by his father's house (Numbers 1:18). A man who could not show it was set aside (Ezra 2:59). The one Davidic house Luke assigns in the birth account is Joseph's (Luke 2:4). The only kin Luke gives Mary is of Aaron (Luke 1:5, 36). So the "evident" descent from Juda (Hebrews 7:14) is reckoned through Joseph.

**C3. The father is named in four registers.**

- **[L1]** Mary speaks in Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The Greek is *ho patēr sou* (G3962), "thy father."
- **[L3]** The narrator writes "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41). The Greek is *goneis*, "parents."
- **[L3]** The town asks: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42). A disciple says: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- **[L3]** The angel speaks in Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The 1611 margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]." Matthew 1:21 adds: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Naming the child is the father's act, as in Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."

**C4. The means of begetting is knowing, and the abstinence is bounded.**

- **[L1]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." The Hebrew is *yada'* (H3045), "know."
- **[L3]** Joseph and Mary are husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19) and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The Greek is *heōs hou* (G2193), "till." It is joined to *eginōsken*, the imperfect of *ginōskō* (G1097).
- **[L4]** The seed must come out of a man's loins (C1). The text's stated means of begetting is a husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1). Joseph is husband in law from the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24). The abstinence of Matthew 1:25 is bounded by "till," which covers the pregnancy. So I hold that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal. The child is of his loins, and Christ had a biological father.

---

## PRESSES ON THE DEFENDER'S CHAIN

### LINK D1: "the conception preceded any coming together"

**Luke 1:34 is present tense, and the conception is future to it.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The Greek is *andra ou ginōskō*. This is the present indicative of *ginōskō* (G1097). It states her condition at the moment the angel spoke.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31 comes before it: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." The Greek is *syllēmpsē*, a future tense. The conception lies ahead of the words of 1:34.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:27 says the virgin was "espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." The man to whom she is bound is named in the same verse that calls her *parthenos* (G3933).

**Matthew defines "came together" by what follows.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." The Greek is *synelthein* (G4905).
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:24 tells us what the coming together was: Joseph "took unto him his wife." The Greek is *parelabe* (G3880), "took to himself." The law names the same step in Deuteronomy 20:7: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:18 dates the finding before the taking (1:24). Matthew 1:25 covers the time after the taking. The order Matthew gives is the espousal, then the finding, then the taking, then the "till." That fits C4, a union within the espousal.

**Genesis 4:1 supports my side.**

The defender's own [L3], Genesis 4:1 ("Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"), names a husband's knowing as the means. That is the footing of C4.

### LINK D2: "of the Holy Ghost" as the begetter

**The verse is quoted whole.** Matthew 1:20 reads: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The 1611 margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]." The angel's "for" (*gar*) gives the reason to *take his wife*. The same row names "thou son of David."

***Ek* with God, and *gennaō*, are said of believers who have fathers.**

- **[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." The 1611 margin reads "[is born: Gr. has been born]." The Greek is *ek tou theou gegennētai*, the same *ek* (G1537) and *gennaō* (G1080) the defender reads as paternity.
- **[L3]** 1 John 3:9: "Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him." The 1611 margin reads "[is born: or, has been born]."
- **[L4]** Believers "born of God" each have a man for a father (1 John 5:1; 3:9). So *ek* + *gennaō* + God names a divine origin that stands beside a human father. It does not replace him. Matthew 1:20 joins that origin to "Joseph, thou son of David" in one sentence.

**Luke 1:35's verbs are the verbs of power and presence.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- **[L2]** "Come upon" is *eperchomai* (G1904). The same verb is used in Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The margin there reads "[power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]." It is said of the apostles.
- **[L2]** "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (G1982). The same verb is used of the cloud in Luke 9:34 ("there came a cloud, and overshadowed them") and of Peter's shadow in Acts 5:15 ("that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them").
- **[L4]** Both verbs mean God's power and presence resting on people (Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34; Acts 5:15). Luke 1:35 uses the same two verbs of Mary.

**The "therefore" reaches back to Luke 1:32.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the father David are given in 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in 1:34.
- **[L2]** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The verb is *klēthēsetai*, "shall be called." It is a naming verb.
- **[L3]** The title stands beside a human father in 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." David is the begetter and God is father by covenant, in one verse.
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3-4 joins the two: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared [to be] the Son of God with power ... by the resurrection from the dead." The 1611 margin reads "[declared: Gr. determined]."

### LINK D3: Joseph as "supposed" father only

**Matthew 1:16's passive names the mother, as "born of women" does of men with named fathers.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The Greek is *ex hēs egennēthē*, the passive of G1080 with the feminine "of whom."
- **[L3]** Matthew 11:11 uses the same phrase: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L4]** "Born of" a woman names the mother in the case of a man whose father is named (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13). Matthew 1:16 gives Mary that place. The same chapter calls Joseph "thou son of David" (1:20).
- The defender's step "is not said to be begotten by Joseph" counts what the verse leaves unsaid. My answer rests on what the verses state.

**Luke 3:23: *nomizō* is the custom-and-law verb.**

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** The word is *enomizeto* (G3543). The lexicon gives: "properly, to do by law (usage)." The same form appears in Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made."
- **[L3]** Numbers 1:18 sets the usage of reckoning: "declared their pedigrees ... by the house of their fathers."
- **[L4]** Luke reckons the son "as was supposed," that is, by the established usage of pedigree (Acts 16:13; Numbers 1:18). Luke's own voice is "his parents" (2:41), and Mary's voice is "thy father" (2:48).

**Matthew 1:19 states intent and its grounds.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** "Was minded" is *eboulēthē* (G1014), "to will, intend." The two grounds are *dikaios*, "just," and *mē thelōn paradeigmatisai*, "not willing to make a public example."
- **[L3]** The angel answers the man's *fear*: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). He sends him to take her, and Joseph does: "took unto him his wife" (1:24).
- **[L4]** What 1:19 states is intent and the grounds of a just man. The remedy given is fear removed and his wife taken (1:20, 24). That fits a husband claiming his wife.

**Luke 2:48-49: two fathers in two verses, as in 1 Chronicles 28:6.**

- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:51: "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them."
- **[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." This is said of David's son.
- **[L4]** The defender's Luke 2:49 names the covenant Father (2 Samuel 7:14). Luke 2:48 names Joseph, and 2:51 sets the child "subject unto them." Both fathers stand, as with Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:6).

### LINK D4: "her seed" and Isaiah 7:14

**"Her seed" and "thy seed" are said of women whose sons have named fathers.**

- **[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed."
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son ... For God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel." Eve calls Seth her seed, and Adam is his father.
- **[L3]** Genesis 16:10 to Hagar: "I will multiply thy seed exceedingly." The father is given in Genesis 16:15: "And Hagar bare Abram a son."
- **[L2]** The word is *zera'* (H2233). The same word is attached to a woman in each verse.

**Isaiah's sign stands in its own chapter with a man's approach.**

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The 1611 margin reads "[shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]."
- **[L2]** The word is *'almah* (H5959). The KJV renders it "maid" (Exodus 2:8: "And the maid went and called the child's mother") and "damsels" (Psalm 68:25), as well as "virgin" (Genesis 24:43).
- **[L3]** The sign is bounded in Isaiah's day: "before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good" (Isaiah 7:16). The next sign child comes this way: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son" (Isaiah 8:3). The 1611 margin reads "[went: Heb. approached]." The name recurs in 8:8: "O Immanuel."
- **[L4]** Isaiah's own sign children come by a man going unto the woman (Isaiah 8:3), within the bound of 7:16. Matthew applies the sign to Mary (Matthew 1:22-23), whom the text calls "espoused to a man whose name was Joseph" (Luke 1:27) and "his wife" (Matthew 1:24). The sign and its fulfilment both stand with a husband.

### LINK D5: "a body hast thou prepared me"

**God's preparing of a body stands with a father in the same books.**

- **[L3]** Psalm 139:13: "thou hast covered me in my mother's womb." This is said by David, son of Jesse.
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 1:5: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee." This is said to Jeremiah, "the son of Hilkiah" (Jeremiah 1:1).

**[L2] The verb is *katartizō* (G2675).** It is the verb of Hebrews 11:3: "the worlds were framed by the word of God." God frames bodies through the means he appoints.

**[L1] Hebrews 2:14-17 sets the mode.**

- Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same."
- Hebrews 2:16: "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham." The 1611 margin reads "[took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]."
- Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren."

**[L4]** The body is prepared by God (Hebrews 10:5). It is taken "likewise," "in all things ... like unto [his] brethren" (Hebrews 2:14, 17). It comes "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). That fits a body begotten as his brethren's were.

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

**1. LINK D1.** Defender: "Mary says she has not known a man, and Luke calls her a virgin. So the conception that follows was not by a man's seed."

- ASSUMES: Mary's present state in Luke 1:34 governs the time of the conception. ROWS GIVE: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" (Luke 1:31); "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph" (Luke 1:27); "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1).
- PRESSED WITH: Luke 1:31 [L1] with *syllēmpsē*, future [L2]; Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife" [L3] with *parelabe* (G3880) [L2].

**2. LINK D2.** Defender: "The text thus gives a source for the begetting, and that source is not a human father."

- ASSUMES: *ek* + *gennaō* with God names the man-replacing begetter. ROWS GIVE: "born of God ... him that begat ... begotten of him" (1 John 5:1), said of believers; "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).
- PRESSED WITH: 1 John 5:1 [L3] with G1537/G1080 [L2]; Acts 1:8 [L3] with *eperchomai* (G1904) [L2]; Luke 1:32 [L1] with *dio kai* [L2]; 1 Chronicles 28:6 [L3].

**3. LINK D3.** Defender: "That shows he had no knowledge of having fathered the child."

- ASSUMES: Joseph's intent in Matthew 1:19 arose from his knowledge of the child's origin. ROWS GIVE: "being a just [man] ... was minded to put her away privily" (Matthew 1:19), with *eboulēthē* (G1014), "intend"; "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24).
- This [L4] exhibits only [L1] footing, Matthew 1:19-20, and a single layer kind.
- PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:20 "fear not" [L3]; Deuteronomy 22:24 "his neighbour's wife" [L3].

**4. LINK D3.** Defender: "The text marks Joseph's fatherhood as a supposition and does not state it as a fact."

- ASSUMES: *enomizeto* carries a verdict against the reckoning. ROWS GIVE: "where prayer was wont to be made" (Acts 16:13), the same form; "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
- PRESSED WITH: Numbers 1:18 [L3]; Luke 2:41 "his parents" [L3].

**5. LINK D4.** Defender: "The sign is a virgin conceiving, so the prophecy needs no human father."

- ASSUMES: the word "virgin" in the sign sets the means of conception. ROWS GIVE: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived" (Isaiah 8:3), margin "Heb. approached"; "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son ... another seed" (Genesis 4:25); "the maid went and called the child's mother" (Exodus 2:8), with H5959.
- PRESSED WITH: Isaiah 7:16 [L3]; Genesis 16:10 with 16:15 [L3].

**6. LINK D5.** Defender: "Together they show the body came by God's preparation and not by a father's begetting."

- ASSUMES: God's preparing a body sets aside a father's begetting. ROWS GIVE: "thou hast covered me in my mother's womb" (Psalm 139:13), said by David son of Jesse; "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3); "likewise took part of the same" (Hebrews 2:14).
- PRESSED WITH: Jeremiah 1:5 [L3]; Hebrews 2:16 with its margin [L3]; *katartizō* at Hebrews 11:3 [L2].

**7. LINK D6 (keystone).** Defender: "Christ had no biological father."

- This stands on D1 to D5, each pressed above.
- PRESSED WITH: 2 Samuel 7:12 [L1] with *zera'* (H2233) [L2]; Acts 2:30 [L3] with *osphys* (G3751) [L2]; Romans 1:3 [L3] with *spermatos* (G4690) [L2]; Luke 2:4 [L3].

---

## QUESTION TO THE DEFENDER

According to Hebrews 7:14, "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." Given the law, "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18; see also Numbers 1:2), how is it evident? Answer from the rows, with book, chapter and verse.
