CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 2, CLOSING AND PREMISE LIST

# CHALLENGE, ROUND 2 (CLOSE): The seed is David's according to the flesh, and the father the text names is Joseph

The defender has narrowed the case in three places:

- He withdrew D5 "as an independent proof."
- He withdrew the D3 phrase that Joseph "had no knowledge of having fathered the child."
- He granted that Genesis 3:15 "alone does not settle the means."

The keystone D6 now rests on D1 to D3, and on a new line for Mary: "Luke 3:23-31 and Ezra 2:61 are the footing for Mary's line, and that is an [L4]." I answer each of these at the word, and I close.

---

## 1. Hebrews 7:14 and the house: the defender's own witness carries its verdict

**What the defender holds.** The descent is "met by the house" and needs no begetting by Joseph. The rows he quotes give more than a house.

- **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- **[L2]** *Kata sarka* means "according to the flesh." *Sarx* (G4561) is "flesh." *Osphys* (G3751) is "loins; procreative power."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3 has the same words: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The noun there is *sperma* (G4690), "seed."
- **[L4]** The oath sets the throne-heir "according to the flesh" and "of the fruit of his loins" (Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3). A reckoning by house usage meets the house. The oath names the flesh and the loins as well. So "evident" (Hebrews 7:14) stands on the flesh-seed, reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).

**What Ezra 2:61 says when read with the next verse.** The defender cites Ezra 2:61, a man "called after their name," for a reckoning through the wife's house.

- **[L1]** Ezra 2:61: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name."
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:62 follows at once: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- **[L2]** The house is *bayith* (H1004), "house, family." The father is *'ab* (H1), "father." These are the words of Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers."
- **[L4]** The text records a house reckoned through the wife's father (Ezra 2:61), and the next verse puts that register out (Ezra 2:62). The witness therefore holds to the father's house (Numbers 1:18). That fits C2.

## 2. "Mary's line" (Luke 3:23-31) gives Joseph's name, not hers

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary." The house phrase stands with "a man whose name was Joseph."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:4, of Joseph: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)".
- **[L4]** Luke's register joins Heli to "Joseph" (3:23). Luke's two house rows join David to Joseph (1:27; 2:4). Mary's name stands in 1:27 with "espoused," and her kin in 1:36 is "thy cousin Elisabeth," of "the daughters of Aaron" (1:5).

The two registers for Joseph, Jacob (Matthew 1:16) and Heli (Luke 3:23), stand as the text gives them. I add no institution to join them. On 2 Chronicles 22:11 I grant the point: a king's daughter married a priest. So I rest C2 on Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4, which name the house on Joseph.

## 3. D1: the virgin at the word, the wife in the espousal

**Granted.** Luke 1:34 is a present state, and the conception is future to it (Luke 1:31, *syllambanō*, G4815, "to conceive"). Genesis 24:16 defines "virgin" at the time it is spoken, and Luke 1:34 is that time.

**The angel's own example of "with God nothing shall be impossible" is a conception by a husband.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:36-37: "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age ... For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
- **[L4]** The "also" sets Mary's conception beside Elisabeth's (1:36). Elisabeth's conception is by "thy wife ... bear thee a son," Zacharias her husband (1:13). The verse "with God nothing shall be impossible" (1:37) follows directly on that example. So the "how" the angel gives stands with a husband's son.

**Before the taking is inside the espousal, where she is his wife.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband."
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." This is said of the betrothed damsel. The word is *rea'* (H7453), "neighbour."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:5: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."
- **[L4]** The defender says the conception came before the taking (Matthew 1:18, 24). The text calls her a wife from the espousal (Matthew 1:19; Deuteronomy 22:24; Luke 2:5). So the time before the taking is the time when she is Joseph's wife. "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1) is the canon's stated means. "Knew her not till she had brought forth" (Matthew 1:25) covers the time from the taking to the birth. So I hold, at [L4] on these rows, that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

## 4. D2: "of the Holy Ghost" in its own row, and the "therefore"

**The begetting verb with God has people with fathers as its object.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The 1611 margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]."
- **[L2]** The verb is *gennaō* (G1080). The lexicon gives "properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother." The row's "in her" is the mother's side of that gloss.
- **[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." Here God is the subject of *gennaō*, and the objects are believers born of fathers.
- **[L4]** God "begat" men who have fathers (1 John 5:1), with the same verb. The *gar* of Matthew 1:20 grounds the command "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife," and the same row names "thou son of David." So the origin clause stands beside the husband the row commands.

**The flesh is born of the flesh.**

- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3 sets the flesh in David's seed: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The flesh comes of the seed according to the flesh, and the Spirit's work is of the Spirit.

**The "result" of Luke 1:35 is a naming.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:35 says the result is "shall be called the Son of God." The verb is *kaleō* (G2564), "to call, name."
- **[L2]** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:32: "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the throne are given before Mary asks "How shall this be" (1:34).
- **[L3]** "This day have I begotten thee" is set at its three New Testament occasions:
  - the resurrection, in Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee";
  - the priesthood, in Hebrews 5:5: "Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee";
  - beside 2 Samuel 7:14, in Hebrews 1:5: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"
- **[L3]** Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power ... by the resurrection from the dead." The 1611 margin reads "[declared: Gr. determined]."
- **[L4]** The title's begetting-word is applied at the resurrection and the priesthood (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 5:5; Romans 1:4). In Luke the title travels with "the throne of his father David" (1:32). So 1:35's "shall be called" names the covenant Son, as with "Solomon thy son ... my son" (1 Chronicles 28:6).

## 5. D3 and D4: the father's acts, and the sign child of Isaiah's day

**Naming is a father's act as well as a mother's.**

- **[L1]** The angel speaks to Joseph in Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." It is done in Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
- **[L3]** The angel speaks to Zacharias in Luke 1:13: "thou shalt call his name John."
- **[L4]** The angel lays the same charge on a named father in Luke 1:13 and on Joseph in Matthew 1:21. Mary's own word is "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48, *patēr*, G3962), and the narrator's word is "his parents" (Luke 2:41).

**Isaiah's sign child has a father and a mother.**

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:3-4: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son ... For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother." The 1611 margin at 8:3 reads "[went: Heb. approached]."
- **[L2]** The word is *'almah* (H5959). The KJV renders it "the maid" in Exodus 2:8 ("And the maid went and called the child's mother").
- **[L4]** The sign is bounded in Isaiah's day (7:16). The sign child of chapter 8 cries "My father, and my mother" (8:4). Matthew applies the sign to a woman "espoused to a man whose name was Joseph" (Luke 1:27). So the sign and its fulfilment both stand with a husband.

## 6. Close

The seed promised to David proceeds "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). The loins are the father's members: "they come out of the loins of Abraham" (Hebrews 7:5) and "he was yet in the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:10). Luke sets the house of David on Joseph (Luke 1:27; 2:4). Mary calls him "thy father" (Luke 2:48). The angel names him "thou son of David" in the same row as "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The Holy Ghost's verbs are power and presence (Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34). The begetting-title is set at the resurrection (Acts 13:33; Romans 1:4). Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David.

- [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." In one verse, the son David begat bears the covenant title.
- [L3] 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." Here "of God" marks an origin that is covenant, not flesh.
- [L4] "Of the Holy Ghost" in Matthew 1:20 stands in the same row as "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife." The defender granted that the "for" grounds the command to take her.

**5. The union, read inside the chain.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") at Luke 1:34 is present. *syllambanō* (G4815, "to conceive") at Luke 1:31 is future. The defender granted both.
- [L3] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife." Deuteronomy 22:24: "his neighbour's wife." Deuteronomy 20:7: "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- [L3] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L4] The seed must come out of a man's loins (Acts 2:30), and the stated means of conceiving is a husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1). The one man named is "her husband" from the espousal (Matthew 1:19). "Till" bounds the not-knowing to the time from the taking to the birth.
- So I hold, footed on these rows, that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

**6. The sign of Isaiah stands in its own day.**
- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"
- [L2] *'almah* (H5959) is the word the KJV renders "the maid" at Exodus 2:8 and "the damsels" at Psalms 68:25. The defender granted this.
- [L3] Isaiah 7:16 bounds the sign: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings." Isaiah 8:3 follows: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son... [went: Heb. approached]." Isaiah 8:8 names the land: "thy land, O Immanuel."
- [L4] The sign is set in Isaiah's generation, with a husband's approach beside its conceiving. Matthew 1:22-23 applies it, and Isaiah 8:3 shows the shape of its fulfilling.

**The close.**
- [L1] Hebrews 2:16: "but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]"
- [L3] Hebrews 2:17: "Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren." Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same."
- [L4] He was made like his brethren in all things and took part of flesh and blood "likewise." His flesh is "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3), out of the loins (Acts 2:30). His tribe is evident by the fathers' house (Hebrews 7:14; Numbers 1:18), and his father is named by his mother (Luke 2:48) and by the angel: "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
- Christ had a biological father: Joseph, of the house and lineage of David.
